_comment: Lane -> ROLE -> Chrome deviceId. Read by scripts/chrome-pin.sh.
WHY ROLES AND NOT A SINGLE PIN PER LANE: several lanes need a PRIMARY session plus
occasional access to a shared one (journal access). A lane therefore has one primary
role and a list of alternates it may switch to with select_browser.
MECHANISM (Claude Code v2.1.259, read from the binary): the MCP prompts only when the
GLOBAL pin (~/.claude.json .chromeExtension.pairedDeviceId) matches no connected browser.
A matching pin auto-connects silently. selectedDeviceId is PER-PROCESS, so a lane may
call select_browser for an alternate without disturbing any other lane's routing.
requirePairedDevice exists in the binary but is never provided by the CLI: unusable.
DEVICE IDs ARE DELIBERATELY null WHERE UNVERIFIED. Two extensions are connected
(da3bf06e... 'Browser 1', b72a12c5... 'Browser 2') but which profile each one IS has
NOT been established. Evidence so far: only two Chrome profiles exist -- Default
naca028@expert.micro1.ai) -- and Arc, Brave, Chromium, Edge and Firefox are also
installed, any Chromium one of which can carry the extension. No profile named for BYU
or journal access was found, so the library session lives inside one of these or in a
browser not yet connected. Run `chrome-pin.sh resolve` for how to settle it.
GUESSING HERE WOULD SEND AN ARCHON'S CREDENTIALED WORK INTO THE WRONG SESSION.

snorkel.evidence: W13:Jacques reported 'Browser 2: Authenticated Snorkel session' on 2026-09-09 -- a browser LABEL, not a verified profile.

micro1.evidence: Chrome 'Profile 1' is named expert.micro1.ai (naca028@expert.micro1.ai). Which deviceId serves it is unverified.

library.purpose: BYU library / journal access. Carries the cookies and session for bulk literature download. SHARED: several lanes borrow it.
library.evidence: NOT LOCATED. No Chrome profile is named for it. Likely inside the Default profile or in another installed browser.

general.purpose: Ordinary browsing with no credentialed session to protect. Lanes using this should OPEN A NEW WINDOW rather than adopt whatever is on screen.
general.evidence: Default profile ('Your Chrome') is the natural candidate.
